title: 2025年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2025年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying. But what about those of us who don't have a natural talent? We've been told all our lives that if you work hard, you too can succeed. But with the release of Angela Duckworth's Grit, we are given a new key to success.

P2 "As much as talent counts, effort counts twice," says Duckworth in Grit. She introduces a new concept that talent may be overrated, and if you want real success, what you need is grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence. Even if you have natural talent, it's nothing without grit.

P3 Duckworth says grit is the difference between success and failure. A person who has grit is more likely to succeed than a person who does not. When we think about attaining success—whether it's landing that job or learning that new skill—our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn. If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part—and you must be perfect at all of them. Grit is different because it tells us that perfection isn't the goal.

P4 Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders. Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible. Grit allows us to redefine our goals. Think about it: what's something you've always wanted to do, but gave up because you "don't have the skills for it"? What's something you love but aren't good at?

P5 The real workings of grit are to have sustainable passion and continue to try. Effort means more than your natural ability. Even if you haven't mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed if you can transform your passion into action. In a way, Duckworth is giving new hope to people who have shut the doors on their dreams. She is saying it is possible that you can accomplish anything. If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit.

questions.q: What does the passage say about people born with natural talents?
options: They seem to outdo others without hard work.
They appear to know all the secrets to success.
They feel it only too logical to succeed.
They are bound to excel effortlessly.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about people born with natural talents 直接问文章对一个 具体对象的陈述，没有 infer/imply/mainly about 这类字眼，是典型细节复述题。

【拆句】主干是 What does the passage say about people，过去分词短语 born with natural talents 作后置定语修饰 people，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What does the passage say about people born with natural talents? A) They seem to outdo others without hard work. B) They appear to know all the secrets to success. C) They feel it only too logical to succeed. D) They are bound to excel effortlessly.

【定位】With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying. 对于那些天生有才的人，看上去就好像他们不太费力就能出类拔萃。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 it feels as if they excel without really trying ↔ They seem to outdo others without hard work 预判的「看似/不费力/胜过别人」三个语义点在 A 中一一落位，无增项无漏项，A 是定 位句的同义改写。 B) 无中生有 原文只说他们看似不费力就出色，没说他们 know all the secrets to success——「掌 握所有成功秘诀」是凭空添加的内容。 C) 偷换概念 原文是「看上去毫不费力就成功」，选项却说 They feel it only too logical to succeed ——「他们觉得自己成功理所当然」是从他们的主观视角描写，与原文「旁观者眼中显 得轻松」不一致。 D) 过度推断 原文只用 it feels as if（似乎）表达印象，选项却用 are bound to（必然、注定）把可 能性写成必然性，过度推断。 Duckworth 对才能有何看法? A) 这是一个被过分高估的新概念。 B) 它被证明对于重大成就是必要的。 C) 它在一个人的成功中起较小的作用。 D) 它是人生真正成功的保证。

questions.q: What does Duckworth say about talent?
options: It is a new concept much too overrated.
It proves necessary for big achievements.
It plays a lesser role in one's success.
It is a guarantee for real success in life.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Duckworth say about talent 问的是特定人物对特定对象的陈述，是细节题。

【拆句】结构与 51 题平行：What does Duckworth say about talent，主谓宾完整，无修饰 从句。

【定位】As much as talent counts, effort counts twice. 虽然才能很重要，但努力的重要性是它的两倍。 52. What does Duckworth say about talent? A) It is a new concept much too overrated. B) It proves necessary for big achievements. C) It plays a lesser role in one's success. D) It is a guarantee for real success in life.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 It is a new concept much too overrated 把 She introduces a new concept 中「新 概念」的所指对象——其实是 grit——硬安到 talent 头上；原文说的「新概念」指 grit，而非 talent。 B) 与原文相反 原文反复说 talent 不够、需 grit 加持（Even if you have natural talent, it's nothing without grit）；选项却说 talent proves necessary for big achievements，是反向 陈述。 C) ✓ 正确 As much as talent counts, effort counts twice ↔It plays a lesser role in one's success talent may be overrated ↔plays a lesser role 预判的「才能不如努力重要、被高估」与 C 的「作用较小」在比较义上完全等值，C 正确。 D) 与原文相反 原文称 grit 才是 real success 的关键（if you want real success, what you need is grit），选项却说 talent is a guarantee for real success，把被弱化的对象说成「保 证」，方向与程度同时反了。 文章对想要获得成功的人有何评价? A) 他们困惑于如何向雇主展示自己最好的一面。 B) 他们被自己对完美的期望所困扰。 C) 他们会努力找到最适合自己技能的工作。 D) 他们会发现自己缺乏所需的所有技能。

questions.q: What does the passage say about people thinking of attaining success?
options: They are puzzled how to present their best to the employer.
They are burdened by their expectation of perfection.
They will try hard to land a job that fits their skills best.
They will find themselves lacking in all the skills they need.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about people thinking of attaining success 仍是 say 句 型，针对一个具体场景，是细节题。

【拆句】主干仍是 What does the passage say about people，现在分词短语 thinking of attaining success 作后置定语修饰 people；其中 attaining 是动名词作 of 的宾语，整体 「想着去获得成功的人」。 53. What does the passage say about people thinking of attaining success? A) They are puzzled how to present their best to the employer. B) They are burdened by their expectation of perfection. C) They will try hard to land a job that fits their skills best. D) They will find themselves lacking in all the skills they need.

【定位】When we think about attaining success—whether it's landing that job or learning that new skill—our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn. If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part—and you must be perfect at all of them. 当我们考虑获得成功时——不管是拿下那份工作还是学会某项新技能——我们的思绪立刻被 「必须先学会的所有东西」压得沉甸甸的。如果你想要那份新工作，你得学工作技能，然后 学面试技巧，再学穿衣得体——而且你必须在每一项上都做到完美。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 They are puzzled how to present their best to the employer 把原文里「找工作」举 例中的「dress part/interview skills」放大成全部困扰，且把 burdened 改成 puzzled ——既缩小到一例又改写状态词。 B) ✓ 正确 our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn ↔ They are burdened by their expectation of perfection 预判要求「负担 + 完美」两点齐备，B 正好同时命中——burdened 锁住「负担」， expectation of perfection 锁住「完美主义」。 C) 与原文相反 原文是「想成功的人感到被各种要求压垮」，选项却说他们 will try hard to land a job that fits their skills best——把焦虑负担改写成积极行动，方向反了。 D) 过度推断 原文说他们意识到要学很多东西，选项却说他们 lacking in all the skills they need ——把「要学的东西多」推到「所有技能都欠缺」，all 是绝对化程度词，原文未明说 欠缺。 作者认为毅力如何对我们有帮助? A) 它让我们知道自己擅长什么。 B) 它为我们打开了新机会的眼界。 C) 它使我们的注意力集中在所做的事情上。 D) 它让我们重新考虑要实现的目标。

questions.q: How does the author think grit can be helpful to us?
options: It allows us to know what we are good at.
It opens our eyes to new opportunities.
It focuses our attention on what we do.
It lets us reconsider the goals to achieve.
questions.explain:
【判型】How does the author think grit can be helpful to us 问的是 grit 的具体作用，不是隐含 推断，是细节题。

【拆句】How does the author think grit can be helpful to us 是宾语从句嵌套结构：think 后接 省略 that 的从句 grit can be helpful to us，how 修饰整个 think 的方式逻辑——实际问 的是「作者认为 grit 以何种方式有帮助」。 54. How does the author think grit can be helpful to us? A) It allows us to know what we are good at. B) It opens our eyes to new opportunities. C) It focuses our attention on what we do. D) It lets us reconsider the goals to achieve.

【定位】Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders. Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible. Grit allows us to redefine our goals. grit 把不合理的期待从我们肩上卸下来。grit 告诉我们这扇门比我们最初以为的开得更宽。 grit 允许我们重新定义自己的目标。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文从未说 grit 让我们 know what we are good at（知道自己擅长什么）；P4 反而提 到「你一直想做但因『没技能』就放弃的事」，强调 grit 让你即便不擅长也去做，与 「让你知道擅长什么」无关。 B) 过度推断 原文比喻 the door is open wider than we first thought possible，意思是给我们的 可能性变多；选项 opens our eyes to new opportunities 把「门开宽」改成「让我们 看见新机会」——「打开眼界」是额外添加的动作，原文只说门更宽、未说我们因此看 见了新机会。 C) 无中生有 原文 Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders 是卸下「必须样样 完美」的负担，而非聚焦注意力；选项 focuses our attention on what we do 与「卸 担」无关，反而像「让你更专注」。 D) ✓ 正确 Grit allows us to redefine our goals ↔It lets us reconsider the goals to achieve let / reconsider / goals to achieve 三处都能在原文第三句找到一一对应，D 是 Grit allows us to redefine our goals 的同义改写。 Duckworth 在她的《坚毅》一书中试图传达什么信息? A) 我们应该完善自己以确保成功。 B) 我们应该即使面对失败也要坚持不懈。 C) 没有持续练习,我们永远无法掌握一项技能。 D) 没有热情,我们永远无法期望达到目标。

questions.q: What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit?
options: We should perfect ourselves to ensure success.
We should stay persistent even in face of failures.
We can never master a skill without constant practice.
We can never expect to reach our goals without passion.
questions.explain:
【判型】What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit 问的是整本书的核心信 息，是典型主旨题。

【拆句】What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit：宾语前置 What message，主干 Duckworth try to convey，介词短语 in her book Grit 作地点状语，无 难点。 55. What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit? A) We should perfect ourselves to ensure success. B) We should stay persistent even in face of failures. C) We can never master a skill without constant practice. D) We can never expect to reach our goals without passion.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文反复说 perfection isn't the goal、Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders，明确否定完美主义；选项却让我们 perfect ourselves to ensure success，方向反了。 B) ✓ 正确 If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit ↔ We should stay persistent even in face of failures grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence ↔stay persistent continue to try ↔stay persistent B 同时命中预判的两大语义点——「失败」和「坚持」，是把全文主线压缩到一句话的 最佳改写。 C) 以偏概全 Even if you haven't mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed 恰恰 说「没掌握技能也能成」；选项却把全书主旨说成 never master a skill without constant practice——把「关于 grit 的人生观」缩成「学技能要练习」，既偏题又用了 never 这种绝对化词。 D) 以偏概全 原文虽说 grit = passion + persistence，但全书主旨是「坚持着再试一次」，而非「没 激情就达不到目标」；选项 can never expect to reach our goals without passion 用 never 把 passion 描述为达成目标的「唯一条件」，把成对要素中的一个单独绝对化。
